name: Dermoid or Epidermoid Cyst of the Central Nervous System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for CNS Dermoid/Epidermoid Cysts

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated cystic lesion with characteristic MRI/CT imaging features (e.g., hyperintense on T1 for dermoid, diffusion restriction for epidermoid)
Histopathological confirmation showing cyst lined by squamous epithelium with keratinous debris (epidermoid) or dermal appendages (dermoid)
Neurological symptoms consistent with mass effect or cyst rupture such as headache, seizures, or cranial nerve deficits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging characteristics consistent with dermoid or epidermoid cyst plus histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and confirmed by histopathology after surgical resection or biopsy.

pathognomonic.notes: Occurs due to cyst content spillage causing aseptic meningitis
searchTerms: inflammation of brain lining from cyst rupture

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic diffusion restriction on MRI (epidermoid cyst)
pathognomonic.notes: Highly specific imaging finding for epidermoid cysts
searchTerms: MRI shows restricted diffusion in cyst
characteristic MRI findings of epidermoid cyst

common.symptomName: Chronic headache due to mass effect

common.notes: Focal or generalized seizures may occur

searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
fluid buildup in brain from cyst blockage
brain swelling secondary to cyst obstruction

rare.symptomName: Sudden neurological deterioration due to cyst rupture
searchTerms: sudden neurological decline after cyst rupture
acute brain symptoms from cyst break
brain fluid buildup with optic nerve swelling
increased brain pressure causing eye swelling

laboratory: CSF analysis may show sterile chemical meningitis with elevated protein and inflammatory cells after cyst rupture
imaging: MRI: hyperintense on T1-weighted images for dermoid cysts
MRI: diffusion-weighted imaging shows restricted diffusion in epidermoid cysts
CT: well-defined hypodense or mixed density lesions with possible calcifications
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; typically sporadic
other: Histopathology: cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium with keratin debris (epidermoid) or dermal appendages such as hair follicles and sebaceous glands (dermoid)

distinguishingFeatures: Arachnoid cysts do not show diffusion restriction on MRI
Lack of keratinous debris on histopathology
Craniopharyngiomas often have solid and cystic components with calcifications
Histopathology shows squamous epithelium with wet keratin but also other features

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe headache with meningeal signs indicating cyst rupture
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema and vomiting
references: Osborn AG. Diagnostic Imaging: Brain. 2nd ed. Elsevier; 2015.
Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System. 4th ed. IARC; 2016.
Kumar V, Abbas AK, Aster JC. Robbins Basic Pathology. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
